messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: GPU pressure detected in dedicated pool 'dp-auren-eu-west1' (tenant: Auren LLC). 95% GPU util across pool, enqueued queue length increased x6 over baseline. Impact: tail latency > 2s for realtime endpoints. Paging on-call.

emma (oncall): On it. Confirming: this is a single-tenant dedicated pool for Auren, correct? any autoscale policy on this pool?

Raj S: Confirm - dedicated single-tenant. Autoscale is disabled per contract for Auren (no multi-tenant bursting). Current pool size is 8 A100s, all healthy but saturated.

Lena (CS): Auren is business-critical and on our Enterprise SLA. They explicitly opted out of multi-tenant bursting and no cross-tenant migration. Customer is already on hotline - keep them updated.

Mike I: Quick triage: checking active job queue. I see a bunch of long-running batch jobs from internal backfills and one stuck inference worker retrying. Kicking staging backfills off the pool should be safe to evict.

Sophie ML: Adding model context: Auren is running a large LLM v2.2 with long-context KV cache. Evicting/restarting might flush caches and increase latency briefly. Prefer graceful draining of non-critical tasks.

emma (oncall): Options: 1) Manual burst (allocate spare nodes in eu-west1 into this dedicated pool) 2) Evict internal backfills and throttle Auren's lower-priority jobs (if any) 3) Contact finance/product for one-time approved temporary burst since contract disallows autoscale. Thoughts?

Phil P: From product/legal: contract forbids multi-tenant bursting but allows provider-managed manual burst within same tenancy if customer agrees. Need CS signoff from Lena and explicit customer consent for temporary additional capacity.

Lena (CS): I spoke to Auren rep: they approve a manual temporary capacity add for 2 hours, provided no data leaves VPC and we notify when we scale down. They want a timeline and the exact size.

emma (oncall): Good. Recommend allocate +4 A100s for 2 hours (50% capacity bump). Tech lead approval? :eyes:

Raj S: +4 sounds reasonable. Manual allocation steps: run pool-scale API to attach spare instances -> update routing -> warm up KV caches. Quick commands below:

```bash
# allocate 4 nodes to dedicated pool
redwoodctl pools attach --pool dp-auren-eu-west1 --count 4 --node-type a100
# verify
redwoodctl pools describe dp-auren-eu-west1 | jq .capacity
# warm caches (best-effort)
redwoodctl warmup --pool dp-auren-eu-west1 --model auren/llm-v2.2 --threads 10
```

Mike I: I'll run the attach. I'll evict internal backfills first and then attach. ETA 6-8 min to drain backfills, +3 min to attach.

emma (oncall): Approved by on-call and CS. Phil P, mark as customer-approved temporary burst (2 hours). Finance noted internal OK for emergency costs.

Phil P: Logged approval. Please tag me in the postmortem for chargeback and contract update notes.

Mike I: Evicted non-critical backfills. Running attach now. 1/4 nodes attached... 2/4... 4/4 attached. Pool capacity shows 12 A100s.

Sophie ML: Starting warmup; KV fills are progressing. Latency dropping in traces.

emma (oncall): Monitoring metrics: queue length down 70%, p95 latency back to 320ms. Customer CS notified.

Lena (CS): Auren confirmed improvement and appreciates the quick action. Keep them posted 15 min before scale-down.

emma (oncall): Set timer for 1h45m to warn customer, scale-down at 2h. Also filing an incident ticket for follow-up: root cause analysis and request enabling pre-authorized bursts for Auren to avoid manual approvals.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity reduced to SEV-3 (service restored). Tickets: INC-2026-221. Remind: capture cost delta and update contract options.

Raj S: Postmortem action items: (1) Investigate why internal backfills landed on the dedicated pool (2) Add opt-in pre-authorized temporary burst flag for customers who want faster remediation (3) Improve automated warmup to reduce p95 spike after attach.

emma (oncall): Thanks team. I'll hand off to daytime oncall for post-incident follow-up. Closing live paging. :thumbsup:
